title: Actual chain representatives of derived maps from the top degree
statement: Let A be an abelian category with a chosen derived category [def-weil-abstract-derived-category], let P be an integer cochain complex, and let n be an integer such that P^i=0 for every i>n. For every object X of A and every derived morphism phi:Q(P) -> Q(X[-n]), there is an actual chain map f:P -> X[-n] with Q(f)=phi. Here X[-n] is the single complex in degree n. No projectivity or injectivity hypothesis is imposed.

source.place: Tag 094G, lemma-locally-constant, construction of the final differential from the derived boundary

proof.text: Let P be zero above n. Its outgoing differential d^n is zero, so the canonical homology inclusion H^n(P) -> opcycles^n(P) is invertible. Compose the quotient P^n -> opcycles^n(P) with its inverse to obtain P^n -> H^n(P). Transport H^n(phi) through the comparison between complex and derived homology, and through the homology isomorphism of the target single complex, to obtain a morphism H^n(P) -> X. Its composite with the quotient kills every incoming differential and hence defines a chain map f from P to X in degree n [def-weil-abstract-derived-category].

source.place: Tag 094G, lemma-locally-constant, construction of the final differential from the derived boundary

proof.text: The map f induces exactly the prescribed top homology map. To check this, cancel the epimorphism cycles^n(P) -> H^n(P) and the monomorphism from the target homology to its opcycles. Naturality of the opcycles and homology maps reduces the equality to H^n(P) -> opcycles^n(P) composed with its inverse, followed by the standard single-complex homology isomorphism. These are inverse-isomorphism identities.

source.place: Tag 094G, lemma-locally-constant, construction of the final differential from the derived boundary

proof.text: For the standard t-structure [def-sbc-standard-tstructure-derived-category], Q(P) is <=n and the target single complex is >=n. The generic source-library theorem DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor_map_bijective_of_isLE_of_isGE says H^n is bijective on these morphisms. Its argument uses the truncation projection of the source to >=n and the truncation inclusion of the target from <=n: both induce H^n isomorphisms, and truncation orthogonality gives unique factorization through these maps. The intermediate objects lie in the shifted heart, where the single-complex functor is fully faithful and H^n is its inverse. Thus H^n is injective on the original morphism set. Apply that injectivity to Q(f) and phi, using Step 2 and naturality of the complex-to-derived homology comparison, to get Q(f)=phi.

mathlib_searches.query: For a cochain complex with zero terms above n, every derived morphism to an object placed in degree n is represented by a chain map
mathlib_searches.results: ChainComplex.toSingle₀Equiv and HomologicalComplex.mkHomToSingle construct chain maps, but do not identify arbitrary derived maps with them. DerivedCategory.to_singleFunctor_obj_eq_zero_of_injective has an extra injective-target assumption and a different conclusion.
HomologicalComplex.mkHomToSingle and its component formula; these do not state surjectivity after derived localization.

The chain-map constructor and instances using injective targets; the general derived top-degree chain-representative statement is absent from Mathlib. The source-library homologyFunctor_map_bijective_of_isLE_of_isGE supplies its injectivity step.

theorem exists_chainMap_to_single_of_isStrictlyLE
    {A : Type u} [Category.{v} A] [Abelian A] [HasDerivedCategory.{w} A]
    (P : CochainComplex A ℤ) (n : ℤ) [P.IsStrictlyLE n] (X : A)
    (φ : Q.obj P ⟶ Q.obj ((CochainComplex.singleFunctor A n).obj X)) :
    ∃ f : P ⟶ (CochainComplex.singleFunctor A n).obj X, Q.map f = φ
